deities: Lord Rama (as Raghunath, the Ram avatar of Vishnu)
Lord Hanuman (stone-engraved idol outside the main shrine)

history.summary: The Raghunath Temple of Rampur Bushahr is a stone temple on the town's main road, opposite the Narsingh Temple, dedicated to the Ram avatar of Vishnu (inditales.com). It is described as a similar stone structure to the Narsingh temple, now surrounded by a dharamshala, with a stone-engraved idol of Hanuman outside the main shrine and on its outer walls. One travel guide calls it one of the oldest temples in Rampur (gettoplists.com), but no founder, dynasty or built date is recorded in accessible sources, so its age is unverified. NOTE: do not confuse this shrine with the famous Raghunathji Temple of Kullu (built in the 17th century by Raja Jagat Singh of Kullu) - that is a different, better-documented temple. Coordinates are approximate Rampur-town coordinates (wikimapia: 31 deg 26'59"N 77 deg 37'47"E), since no POI-level position for the shrine was found.

name: Raghunath Temple
town_description: Rampur Bushahr is a historic town on the Sutlej River in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh - the last capital of the Bushahr princely state and a former trading centre on the old Hindustan-Tibet Road, known for Padam Palace and the annual Lavi Fair.

travel.airport: Shimla Airport (Jubbarhatti), about 130 km from Rampur.
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Shimla (narrow-gauge), about 130 km away; Kalka (broad gauge) is farther.
travel.road: On NH-5 (the old Hindustan-Tibet Road), about 130 km from Shimla; regular buses and taxis connect Rampur to Shimla and nearby towns.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November; the Lavi Fair in November is a good time to experience local culture.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online; daytime darshan typical of small-town temples.
